reason: I'll start with the biceps side, using the muscle cells to fill the space between its tendons.
expectation: I expect the cells to form the biceps on the front of the arm, though it may take more steps to finish it.

alternatives.reason: Strengthening the front bone attachment also fits the goal, but I want to build the muscle first.

effect: The muscle cells formed the biceps, but the radius still needs mineral. I'll strengthen that attachment next.
reaction: The picture of muscle cells joining into fibres and pulling to bend the elbow was helpful.
reason: Adding mineral to the front completes the other part of the biceps goal.
expectation: I expect the mineral to harden the radius where the biceps tendon pulls.

alternatives.reason: I could start the triceps, but I want to finish the front first.

effect: The radius now has mineral among its bone fibres, completing the biceps goal. The back of the arm still needs both parts.
reaction: It was useful to see that the mineral stays in the bone, not the tendon or cartilage.
reason: I'll build the triceps next, using the muscle cells in the space on the back of the arm.
expectation: I expect the cells to form the triceps, which the chapter says straightens the elbow.

alternatives.reason: I could strengthen the back bone first, but I want to build the muscle before adding mineral.

effect: The triceps is in place and straightens the elbow by pulling behind it; the ulna still needs mineral.
reaction: The contrast with the biceps made the different pull directions clear.
reason: I'll use the only offered combination to strengthen the back bone attachment.
expectation: I expect mineral to harden the ulna and complete the triceps goal.

effect: The ulna now has mineral among its bone fibres, completing the triceps goal and the chapter.
reaction: The result was clear, though similar to adding mineral to the radius.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps after the biceps was most worthwhile: seeing their pulls on opposite sides explained how the same kind of muscle cells can bend or straighten the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral to the second bone felt repetitive after seeing it added to the first, even though both attachments needed strengthening.

surprise.text: The same kind of pulling cells can have opposite effects because of where the muscles attach.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. The goals and pictures explained why each muscle and bone needed its part, although the final combination was the only one offered.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see more connections between body structures and what they do, though I hope there are more choices than the repeated fittings here.
